title: Where to play, how to win with AI
alt: Five meshing gears. Two orange business-strategy gears on the left, labelled Where to play? (strategic positioning of the organisation: geography, markets, customer segments, products, channels) and Strategic priorities (e.g. per value stream), drive a sand-coloured gear in the middle labelled How to win with AI? (where do we see the biggest potential across the core value streams?), which drives two lilac AI-strategy gears on the right labelled Winning capabilities (AI capabilities your organisation must build to scale impact) and Management systems (structures and routines that ensure strategy is consistently executed, owned, governed and improved).
description: The AI strategy framework: business strategy sets where to play and the strategic priorities; AI strategy answers how to win with AI, which capabilities to build and which management systems keep it running. Use it in a strategy or AI-roadmap offer where the drafted alternative would be a lanes or principles section explaining the link between business and AI strategy. Generic: no client data. Has a moving twin: the gears turn on the page.
source: Plainsight AI strategy framework (the gears slide of the strategy deck), redrawn to the slide's layout and colours in the brand fonts with text outlined, 2026-10-24

title: The AI delivery cycle
alt: A wheel of four navy steps around a core labelled Govern, with an orange inner ring labelled Change at the top and Adopt at the bottom. The steps, clockwise from the top left: 01 Value discovery (binoculars), 02 Use case prioritisation (numbered list), 03 Proof of value (thumbs up), 04 Industrialize (plug). Three thin outer arcs name where each part sits: Strategic direction above, AI Lab on the right, AI Factory on the left.
description: How Plainsight identifies, prioritises and delivers AI use cases once strategic direction is set: the four-step cycle with governance at the core and change and adoption running through every step, framed by Strategic direction, the AI Lab and the AI Factory. Use it in an AI strategy, AI Lab or use-case delivery offer where the drafted alternative would be a steps section with four items; write the step descriptions, the emphasis of the moment (which step is done, what change management means in practice) and the handover promise as offer text next to it, not into the picture. Generic: no client data. Has a moving twin: a translucent chevron glides slowly around the cycle.
source: Plainsight AI strategy deck (2026), redrawn to the slide's layout and colours in the brand fonts with text outlined, Tabler outline icons

title: AI readiness per dimension
alt: Six dimensions each with a bar from L1 to L5: strategic direction, data, tools and technology, governance and compliance, organisation and processes, people, skills and culture. A navy bar shows the current level, a peach bar the gap to the target level marked above L3, and an orange circle numbers the priority of four of them: strategic direction first, organisation second, governance third, people fourth. Illustrative values.
description: What the AI readiness scan's per-dimension report looks like, with ILLUSTRATIVE example values: current level, target, and the priority of each gap. Use it in a readiness scan or AI strategy offer to show the shape of the deliverable, with a caption that says the values are an example; never present it as a client's scores. Sharper, deck-drawn successor of ai-maturity-readiness. Has a moving twin: the bars grow in once.
source: Plainsight AI strategy deck (2026), redrawn to the slide's layout and colours in the brand fonts with text outlined, Tabler outline icons

title: The AI readiness ladder with where you stand and the ambition
alt: Five rising steps along an axis labelled Level of AI readiness against ROI: None, Ad hoc and reactive, Aware but fragmented, Structured and focused, Strategic and scalable. An orange pin labelled You're here stands on the second step and a dashed line labelled Ambition leads to an orange flag pin above the fourth. Illustrative positions.
description: The readiness ladder as the scan reports it: five maturity levels with the current position and the ambition marked, ILLUSTRATIVE positions. Use it in a readiness scan or AI strategy offer to explain the levels and the gap in one picture, with a caption that says the pins are an example. Deck-drawn successor of ai-maturity-ladder, which stays for a plain ladder without pins. Has a moving twin: the steps rise once.
source: Plainsight AI strategy deck (2026), redrawn to the slide's layout and colours in the brand fonts with text outlined, Tabler outline icons

title: Crawl, walk, run: the delivery model with a gate between every stage
alt: Three stages along a dashed timeline with an orange decision gate between each. Crawl: assist and display, AI helps and a human decides, low risk, fast learning, an immediate value signal. Gate: technical reliability and trust earned? Walk: advise and route, AI recommends and a human validates, trust deepens, scope widens. Gate: value materialised, ROI measured? Run: autonomous on the happy path, AI acts and humans handle exceptions, earned, not assumed. Closing line: trust earned, not assumed; at every gate the option to stop, pivot or scale stays on the table.
description: The crawl, walk, run delivery model as drawn on plainsight.pro's AI offering page: three stages of autonomy with a go or no-go gate between each. Use it in a build or pilot offer, in the section that explains how a use case is delivered and why every phase ends on a decision (the Blueprint & Build track of the offering); not in a strategy-only offer. Generic: no client data. Has a moving twin: the timeline draws itself, the stages settle in turn and the gates pop; hover a stage or a gate.
source: plainsight.pro AI offering page, public/images/Offering pages/04-crawl-walk-run.svg, redrawn with text outlined in the brand fonts (the pictograms are the page's own), 2026-10-26

title: Federated AI Lab
alt: A central orange circle labelled AI Lab inside a rounded orange frame labelled Federated. Eight navy circles around it, one per department: Sales, Marketing, Finance, Customer Service, Procurement, Operations, HR and IT. A line connects each department to the hub and carries a small orange AI node, the AI expert embedded in that department. Dots between the circles stand for further departments.
description: The federated operating model for AI: a central AI Lab holds the expertise, standards and tooling, and every department has its own embedded AI expert who knows the business. Use it in an offer that proposes an AI Lab or an AI operating model (the AI Lab and operating framework building block) where the drafted alternative would be prose about roles and coordination; name the client's own departments in the text, the picture keeps generic ones. Redrawn from the Embedding AI in your organisation slide of the AI strategy deck; the deck's chosen option badge and pros and cons are left out on purpose.
source: Plainsight AI strategy deck, Embedding AI in your organisation, federated option; redrawn in the brand fonts with the text outlined, 2026-10-26
